issues.description: Check directory name does not match the CheckID in metadata, which will break check discovery/registration
issues.detail: The PR description says the check is `compute_instance_multiple_network_interfaces`, but the directory and files are named `compute_instance_single_network_interface` while the CHANGELOG also references the singular name. Prowler discovers checks by matching the directory/file/class name to `CheckID`. Ensure all four (dir, .py, class, metadata CheckID) are identical, otherwise the check fails to load.

issues.description: GKE exemption via name prefix is brittle and easily bypassed/spoofed
issues.detail: Detecting GKE-managed nodes by `instance.name.startswith("gke-")` is unreliable: custom node pool names, non-default prefixes, or an attacker naming a VM `gke-foo` will all evade or trigger the exemption. Prefer labels (`goog-gke-node`) or the GKE-managed metadata to identify these instances.

issues.description: Zero-interface instances are silently reported as PASS
issues.detail: When `interface_count == 0`, `report.status` remains `"PASS"` even though the status_extended says "has no network interfaces." That is misleading; a VM with zero NICs is an unexpected/edge state and should likely be MANUAL or at least not implicitly PASS. Also, no test covers this branch.

issues.description: Mutable default value on Pydantic model can cause shared-state bugs
issues.detail: `network_interfaces: list[NetworkInterface] = []` in the `Instance` BaseModel uses a mutable default. Pydantic v1 typically copies, but this pattern is fragile and inconsistent with other fields. Use `Field(default_factory=list)` to be safe and match best practice.

issues.description: Service-layer test only weakly verifies new field
issues.detail: `compute_service_test.py` asserts `len(... network_interfaces) == 1` and `== 0` but does not validate that name/network/subnetwork are parsed correctly from the API response (split on `/`, missing fields, etc.). Add an assertion on at least one parsed NetworkInterface's fields to lock in `_get_instances` behavior.

issues.description: Docstring and metadata description disagree on what the check measures
issues.detail: The class docstring describes PASS/MANUAL/FAIL semantics including GKE handling, but the metadata Description and Risk text describe a generic single-NIC requirement with no mention of MANUAL or GKE. Align the metadata Notes/Description with the actual three-state logic so downstream UI/reporting accurately reflects MANUAL outcomes.

review.summary: The PR adds a useful GCP check, but the new directory/files are named `compute_instance_single_network_interface` while the PR title/description claims `compute_instance_multiple_network_interfaces`; if the CheckID and discovery name do not match exactly across class, file, dir, and metadata, the check will not register. The GKE exemption relies on a name prefix that is both bypassable and spoofable; using GKE labels would be more robust. A zero-interface instance is currently reported as PASS with a contradictory message and is untested. Minor concerns: mutable default on the Pydantic model, weak service-layer test coverage for the new `NetworkInterface` parsing, and metadata text that does not describe the MANUAL state.
